'''''Petrorhagia saxifraga''''', known as '''tunic flower''' or '''coat flower''', is a small, herbaceous [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Caryophyllaceae]].<ref name=powo/><ref name=fna/> It is [[native plant|native]] to central and southern Europe, Turkey, the Caucasus, and Iran, and introduced to the United States and Canada, Great Britain, the Baltic States, Poland, and Sweden.<ref name=powo/><ref name=fna/> ''Petrorhagia saxifraga'' is also known as '''tunic saxifrage''', '''pink saxifrage''', or just '''pink'''.<ref name=pf/><ref name=miflora/>

It is a wiry plant with numerous branching stems, narrow leaves, and flowers growing solitary at the ends of branches. The petals range from pink to white.<ref name=fotcr2017/> It is commonly cultivated in rock gardens and used along borders, escaping to grow in lawns, along roadsides, along shorelines, and in other sandy disturbed areas.<ref name=fna/><ref name=miflora/><ref name=fnasubsp/>

Tunic flower was originally [[species description|described]] as ''Dianthus saxifragus'' by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753 and renamed ''Petrorhagia saxifraga'' in 1831.<ref name=ipni1/><ref name=ipni2/> The genus and species name refer to its natural habitat: rock crevices.<ref name=pf/> Two subspecies are accepted:

*''Petrorhagia saxifraga'' subsp. ''gasparrinii'' <small>(Guss.) Pignatti ex Greuter & Burdet</small> – Sicily
*''Petrorhagia saxifraga'' subsp. ''saxifraga'' <small>(L.) Link</small>
